question: How does the yogin mind pleasure and pain outwardly without worldly I-touch?
premises: Pleasure and pain born of contact are minded outwardly, like blue and the rest, as this-shining.
Not as the worldly do, with I-touch, for his is the massed power of self whose universe shines covered with I.
The cited Pratyabhijñā passage confirms the quiescent body-octad knower untouched by pleasure-pain.
inference: Outward minding without I-touch lets the yogin witness pleasure-pain as this-shining.
plain_english: The outward minding of pleasure and pain: born of contact, pleasure and pain are minded outwardly, like blue and the rest, as shining of this — a sensing, not as the worldly do with the touch of I, for his is the massed power of self whose universe shines covered with I, as the cited Pratyabhijñā passage confirms of the quiescent yogin untouched by the two.
